# Name That LLM — Extra API Passages (new prompts) · v1: Claude models

**Synthetic data.** Every passage in this dataset was generated by a large language model through its official API.

This dataset adds fresh labelled paragraphs for the [Name That LLM](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/name-that-llm) competition. The prompts are **new**, written to resemble the style and domain mix of the competition prompts, and they do **not** reuse the competition's training prompts or topics. No competition data (texts, labels or prompts) is included.

v1 covers the **5 Anthropic labels** of the competition, with 1,000 prompts × 5 models = 4,998 passages. Later versions are planned to add the other providers under the same protocol.

## Files
| File | Rows | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ntl_extra_passages_claude.csv` | 4,998 | One passage per (prompt, model). |
| `prompts.csv` | 1,000 | The prompts: `prompt_id`, `domain`, `task_type`, `topic`, `prompt`. |

### Columns of `ntl_extra_passages_claude.csv`
- `id`: stable 12-character id.
- `prompt_id`: joins to `prompts.csv`. Use it as the **group** in cross-validation, because every prompt has one passage per model.
- `model`: label, using the competition's label names: `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`.
- `text`: the passage, a single paragraph.
- `n_words`: number of words in `text`.
- `target_words`: the length requested in the call.
- `domain`, `task_type`, `topic`: copied from the prompt.

## Generation protocol
- **API.** Official Claude API, Message Batches, October 2026. The model ID returned in every response was checked against the requested one: 0 mismatches.
- **Request.** One user message: `<prompt>` followed by `Write a single paragraph of about N words, with no title or headings.`
  - No system prompt.
  - No temperature or thinking parameters, so each model ran with its API defaults.
  - `max_tokens` 8000.
- **Length.** `N` was drawn per (prompt, model) from the empirical word-count distribution of the competition training passages, so the realised lengths look like the competition's: median ~105 words, range ~36–270.
- **Prompts.** 1,000 prompts across physics, biology, philosophy, mathematics, history, creative prose, computer science, psychology, economics and other fields.
  - Task mix: ~57% explain, ~30% describe/narrate, ~7% argue, ~5% story.
  - Deduplicated and checked against the competition's training topics.
- **Cleanup.** Light only: whitespace normalisation and removal of a bold wrapper around a whole passage. Two passages that did not end normally were dropped.

## How close is it to the competition data?
A style classifier was trained **only on the competition train set**: character, word, shape and function-word TF-IDF plus typography counts, with a LinearSVC. Applied to these passages, it assigns the correct **provider** to 68% of them and the exact model to 31%. On grouped cross-validation over the competition train set, the same classifier scores about 70% and 38%. This suggests the passages are close to the competition distribution but not identical to it. The host's exact generation settings (system prompt, reasoning settings, length instruction) are unknown.

## Does it help? (quick ablation)
This ablation uses a style-only model (the TF-IDF + LinearSVC above) with 5-fold cross-validation **grouped by prompt on the competition train set**. The extra passages are added to every training fold only. They never enter validation, and their prompts are disjoint from the train prompts. Sample weights keep each class's total weight equal to its train weight.

| Setting | Balanced accuracy (18-class) | Claude recalls (fable-5 / opus-4-6 / opus-4-8 / opus-5 / sonnet-5) |
|---|---|---|
| train only | 0.383 | 0.13 / 0.53 / 0.21 / 0.66 / 0.41 |
| + these passages (75% of Claude-class weight) | **0.396** | 0.23 / 0.61 / 0.27 / 0.68 / 0.64 |

The GLM classes, which are stylistically close to Claude, lose some recall when only Claude data is added. Adding the other providers should fix this.

## Limitations
- So far only the 5 Claude labels are covered. If you train on this together with the competition data, use per-class weights so the 18-class balance is not distorted.
- The models ran with their API defaults, which may differ from the host's settings.
- Passages are model outputs and can contain factual errors.
